chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture)
subject: cs-10

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an “Elevator Pitch”?

options.B: To quickly pique interest and seek a next step
options.C: To list all technical specifications of a product
options.D: To sign a legal contract immediately

questions.explanation: Option B ('To quickly pique interest and seek a next step') is the verified answer according to Federal Board (FBISE) examination standards for FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture).

questions.question: The “Hook” in a pitch is intended to:

options.B: Grab attention at the very beginning

questions.explanation: Option B ('Grab attention at the very beginning') is the verified answer according to Federal Board (FBISE) examination standards for FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture).

questions.question: Which component of a pitch explains what makes the business unique?
questions.explanation: Option B ('Unique Selling Proposition (USP)') is the verified answer according to Federal Board (FBISE) examination standards for FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture).

questions.question: A business plan is different from a pitch document because it is:
questions.explanation: Option B ('A comprehensive, detailed document (20–40 pages)') is the verified answer according to Federal Board (FBISE) examination standards for FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture).

questions.question: Every elevator pitch should end with a:
questions.explanation: Option C ('Clear “Call to Action”') is the verified answer according to Federal Board (FBISE) examination standards for FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 05 (Unit 8 & Systems Architecture).

questions.question: Which OS manages a network of computers, allowing programs to run on multiple machines simultaneously?
questions.explanation: A Distributed OS allows different computers to work together and share resources.

questions.question: An Operating System integrated into the hardware of a specific device like a microwave oven is called:
questions.explanation: Embedded operating systems are built into devices such as microwaves, washing machines, and smart appliances.

questions.question: What is a "Thread" in the context of a process?

options.B: A basic ordered sequence of instructions within a process

questions.explanation: A thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process.

questions.question: Which process state occurs when a process is waiting for a resource like a printer?
questions.explanation: A process enters the blocked/waiting state when it must wait for a resource.

questions.question: A "Deadlock" occurs when:

options.B: Two or more processes are stuck waiting for each other’s resources

questions.explanation: Deadlock happens when processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.

questions.question: Signals that alert the CPU to events needing immediate attention are called:
questions.explanation: Interrupts notify the CPU about events that require immediate processing.

questions.question: What is software?

options.B: Programs and instructions that tell the computer what to do

questions.explanation: Software is a collection of programs and instructions that enable the computer to perform specific tasks.
